text: dsh-webfetch 是面向 DSH 智能体的网页阅读插件，通过注册七个工具接入 agent：可抓取网页并提取 Markdown 或纯文本、列出页面链接、读取 RSS/Atom 条目、探测 HTTP 响应头与跳转、提取 HTML 表格、读取页面元数据，以及从 robots.txt 和 sitemap 枚举站点 URL。适合需要根据链接阅读资料、整理网页数据或了解站点页面结构的场景。运行需要 Node.js 20 或更高版本；工具使用时由用户提供目标 URL。

dsh-webfetch gives DSH agents seven tools for reading and inspecting web pages: extract Markdown or text, list links, parse RSS or Atom feeds, inspect HTTP headers, extract tables, read metadata, and list site URLs from robots.txt or sitemaps. Users supply a URL; Node.js 20 or later is required.
想让 DSH 把网页正文整理成 Markdown，保留标题和链接。
有没有办法让智能体直接读取我给的网页地址？
帮我从网页里提取纯文本，方便后续总结。
我想快速列出一个页面上的链接并去重。
让 DSH 读取 RSS 或 Atom 订阅源里的最新条目。
怎么把定价页面里的 HTML 表格转成结构化行？
I want my DSH agent to read a URL and return clean page text.
Can I inspect page metadata and discover its canonical URL or feeds?
dsh-webfetch 的功能「网页正文提取」：按 URL 抓取网页并输出 Markdown 或纯文本，可选择同时返回页面链接，并限制提取字符数。
dsh-webfetch 的功能「链接清单」：读取页面中的链接，解析成绝对地址、去重，并按设置的数量上限返回。
dsh-webfetch 的功能「订阅源阅读」：解析 RSS 2.0 或 Atom 地址并返回条目标题、链接、日期等信息，可选包含正文。
dsh-webfetch 的功能「网页表格提取」：将 HTML 表格转换为带列标题的结构化行，可指定表格位置并限制表格数和行数。
dsh-webfetch 的功能「页面信息与站点地图」：读取页面元数据、语言版本和 JSON-LD，或从 robots.txt 与 sitemap 列出站点 URL。

dsh-webfetch README · dsh-webfetch：> 为 DeepSeek Harness 智能体装上「阅读器」：给定 URL，抓取网页并提取干净的 Markdown / 纯文本正文，附带链接清单、RSS/Atom 订阅源解析、HTTP 头部探测、网页表格结构化提取与页面元数据（canonical / Open Graph / hreflang / JSON-LD）读取。零运行时依赖，只读，不发送任何凭证。

dsh-webfetch README · dsh-webfetch：A web page reader plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).
`dsh` agents can search, but until now they could not *read the page behind a URL*.
`dsh-webfetch` closes that gap with seven read-only tools and **zero runtime dependencies** (Node built-ins + global `fetch` only).

dsh-webfetch README · `web_fetch`：| Parameter     | Type                 | Default    | Description                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`         | string (required)    | —          | Full http/https URL of the page to fetch.                      |
| `format`      | `'markdown' \| 'text'` | `markdown` | Markdown keeps headings, links, lists and code fences; `text` is plain prose. |
| `extractLinks`| boolean              | `false`    | Also return every link found on the page (resolved, absolute). |
| `maxChars`    | number               | `50000`    | Cap on extracted content length (1000–200000).                 |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_fetch`：Returns `{ url, finalUrl, status, title, content, length, truncated, links? }`.

```text
user: what does the dsh README say about the architecture?
agent: web_fetch("https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness")
  → HTTP 200 — title: deepseek-harness
    ## DeepSeek Harness

dsh-webfetch README · `web_links`：Collect every link on a page with its visible label, resolved to absolute
URLs, deduplicated, capped at `limit` (1–200, default 50). Useful for mapping
what a page points to or crawling site structure.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_feed`：Read an RSS 2.0 or Atom feed and return its entries as a clean,
LLM-friendly listing. Feed URLs are XML documents that `web_fetch` cannot
extract from — `web_feed` parses them into structured entries instead.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_feed`：| Parameter        | Type              | Default | Description                                                       |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`            | string (required) | —       | Full http/https URL of the RSS or Atom feed.                      |
| `maxItems`       | number            | `10`    | Max entries to return (1–50).                                     |
| `includeContent` | boolean           | `false` | Also return each entry's full content (else summaries only).      |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_feed`：Returns `{ url, finalUrl, status, feedTitle, entryCount, truncated, entries }`,
where each entry is `{ title, url, published?, author?, summary?, content? }`
with CDATA unwrapped, HTML entities decoded, markup stripped and relative
links resolved against the feed URL.

```text
user: what did the example blog post this week?
agent: web_feed("https://blog.example.com/feed.xml", maxItems: 5)
  → feed: Example Blog
    5 entries from https://blog.example.com/feed.xml

dsh-webfetch README · `web_headers`：Inspect the HTTP status, response headers and redirect chain of a URL
**without downloading the page body** — the diagnostic companion to
`web_fetch`: check status codes, content types, redirects, caching or
security headers before (or instead of) pulling the content. Uses `HEAD`
by default and falls back to `GET` automatically when the server answers
405/501; unlike `web_fetch`, *any* status is reported (404/500/… included)
rather than thrown.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_headers`：| Parameter         | Type              | Default | Description                                                              |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `url`             | string (required) | —       | Full http/https URL to inspect.                                          |
| `method`          | `'HEAD' \| 'GET'` | `HEAD`  | `HEAD` downloads no body; `GET` always works but transfers the body.     |
| `followRedirects` | boolean           | `true`  | Follow redirects and report every hop of the chain.                      |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_headers`：Returns `{ url, finalUrl, status, statusText, method, headers, redirects }`
where `headers` is the full response-header map (lower-cased keys) and
`redirects` lists each hop as `{ url, status, location }`.

```text
user: is that download link still alive, and does it redirect?
agent: web_headers("https://example.com/downloads/latest")
  → HTTP 200 OK — HEAD https://example.com/downloads/latest
    redirect chain:

dsh-webfetch README · `web_table`：Extract the HTML tables of a page as **structured rows** — the tables
counterpart of `web_fetch`: spec sheets, pricing pages, comparison charts
and any data locked in `<table>` markup come back as arrays of cell
strings instead of mashed-together prose. The first row is reported as the
header when the page marks it (`<thead>` or an all-`<th>` first row);
`colspan` / `rowspan` are expanded into a rectangular grid with the
spanning text repeated in every covered slot (rows stay self-contained);
nested tables are flattened into the containing cell; cells are
entity-decoded, whitespace-normalized and capped at 200 characters.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_table`：| Parameter   | Type              | Default | Description                                                        |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `url`       | string (required) | —       | Full http/https URL of the page to scan for tables.                |
| `table`     | number            | —       | Return only the table at this 1-based position.                    |
| `maxTables` | number            | `5`     | Max tables to return (1–20).                                       |
| `maxRows`   | number            | `50`    | Max data rows per table (1–200).                                   |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_table`：Returns `{ url, finalUrl, status, tableCount, totalTables, truncated, tables }`
where each table is `{ index, caption, cols, header, rows }` — `rows` is an
array of rows, each an array of cell strings. Tables without any cell are
ignored; `totalTables` counts every non-empty table on the page.

```text
user: pull the tier comparison table off the pricing page
agent: web_table("https://example.com/pricing")
  → 1 table(s) on https://example.com/pricing
    table 1 (3 columns)

dsh-webfetch README · `web_meta`：Read what a page **says about itself**: title, description, canonical URL,
language, charset, robots policy, author, Open Graph and `article:*`
properties, Twitter card tags, hreflang alternates, feed autodiscovery links,
icons and JSON-LD blocks. The metadata counterpart of `web_fetch` — use it to
identify, classify or deduplicate a page, or to discover its feed and language
variants without reading the whole body.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_meta`：| Parameter   | Type              | Default | Description                                          |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`       | string (required) | —       | Full http/https URL of the page to inspect.          |
| `maxJsonLd` | number            | `10`    | Max JSON-LD blocks to return (1–20).                 |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_meta`：Returns `{ url, finalUrl, status, title, description, canonical, lang, charset,
robots, author, openGraph, twitter, alternates, feeds, icons, jsonLd,
jsonLdCount, jsonLdInvalid, truncated }`. Values are reported as written
(entity-decoded, whitespace-normalized, 1000-character cap); `canonical`,
alternate, feed and icon URLs are resolved to absolute. Open Graph and Twitter
entries are ordered `{ name, content }` pairs, so repeated properties (several
`og:image`) survive and exact duplicates collapse. A JSON-LD block that does
not parse is reported as `valid: false` with the parser message and counted in
`jsonLdInvalid` — never silently dropped.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_meta`：```text
user: is this page the canonical English version, and does it have a feed?
agent: web_meta("https://example.com/products/widget")
  → HTTP 200 — metadata of https://example.com/products/widget
    title: Widget — Example

dsh-webfetch README · `web_sitemap`：List a site's **own URLs** from its sitemap — the whole-site counterpart of
`web_links`, which only sees one page. Give it a page, a `robots.txt` or a
sitemap URL: `robots.txt` is read first for its `Sitemap:` directives (falling
back to `/sitemap.xml` when none are published), sitemap **indexes are followed**
to a bounded depth, and every `<url>` comes back with its optional
`lastmod` / `changefreq` / `priority`. Relative `<loc>` values are resolved
against the sitemap URL and duplicates are collapsed.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_sitemap`：| Parameter     | Type              | Default | Description                                                  |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `url`         | string (required) | —       | Full http/https URL: a site page, a `robots.txt` or a sitemap. |
| `maxUrls`     | number            | `100`   | Max URLs to return (1–1000).                                 |
| `maxSitemaps` | number            | `5`     | Max sitemap documents to fetch (1–20).                       |

dsh-webfetch README · `web_sitemap`：Returns `{ url, robotsUrl, robotsStatus, sitemapCount, discovered, urlCount,
truncated, sitemaps, urls }`. `robotsUrl` is `""` when the input was already a
sitemap; `robotsStatus` is the robots.txt HTTP status (`0` when it was missing).
Each entry of `sitemaps` is `{ url, kind, status, entryCount, error }` with
`kind` one of `index`, `urlset`, `gzip` or `error` — a sitemap that fails or is
gzip-compressed is **reported with its reason instead of aborting** the listing,
so a partial inventory is still usable. `discovered` counts every distinct URL
seen (even beyond `maxUrls`), so a capped answer stays honest.

dsh-webfetch README · `web_sitemap`：```text
user: what pages does example.com publish?
agent: web_sitemap("https://example.com/blog")
  → sitemap inventory of https://example.com/blog — robots HTTP 200 (https://example.com/robots.txt)
    sitemap https://example.com/sitemap-index.xml — index HTTP 200, 2 entries

dsh-webfetch README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:TYEclipse/dsh-webfetch

dsh-webfetch README · or a pinned release:：dsh plugin --profile web add github:TYEclipse/dsh-webfetch#v0.6.0
```

Restart your agent session and the tools are available to the model.

dsh-webfetch README · Configuration：All settings are optional (defaults shown):

```yaml
plugins:
  dsh-webfetch:
    timeoutMs: 10000        # per-request timeout (1000–60000)
    maxBytes: 1500000       # response size cap in bytes (10000–5000000)

dsh-webfetch README · Proxy support：Node's built-in `fetch` ignores `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`, so on networks
that require a proxy every request would fail. dsh-webfetch ships a
zero-dependency http-proxy transport (CONNECT tunnelling for https,
absolute-URI form for http, `NO_PROXY` matching with wildcard and IPv4 CIDR
support) and uses it automatically:

dsh-webfetch README · Proxy support：- `httpProxy` / `httpsProxy` (default: `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` env) —
  `http://host:port` URL; set to an empty string to disable.
- `noProxy` (default: `NO_PROXY` env) — comma-separated bypass list
  (exact hosts, `.suffix`, `*.wildcard`, IPv4 CIDRs, optional `:port`).

```yaml
plugins:
  dsh-webfetch:
    httpsProxy: "http://127.0.0.1:7897"   # override env
    noProxy: "localhost,.internal,10.0.0.0/8"

dsh-webfetch README · Proxy support：Proxy credentials embedded in the proxy URL are sent as
`Proxy-Authorization: Basic` (to the proxy only, never to the target).

dsh-webfetch README · Safety model：- **http/https only** — `file:`, `ftp:`, `javascript:` and friends are rejected.
- **No credentials ever** — URLs with embedded credentials are rejected; no
  cookies or authorization headers are attached; nothing is persisted.
- **Bounded everything** — hard timeout per request, redirect hop limit,
  response size cap, extracted-text cap. Oversized bodies are cut off and
  flagged (`truncated: true`), never buffered past the cap.
- **Content-type gated** — `web_fetch`/`web_links` parse only `text/html` and
  `text/plain`; `web_feed` and `web_sitemap` additionally accept
  `application/rss+xml`, `application/atom+xml`, `application/xml` and
  `text/xml` (a `robots.txt` is `text/plain`). Scripts, styles, comments and
  embedded content are stripped by the extractor/parser.
- **Charset-aware** — honours the `Content-Type` charset, falls back to XML
  declaration / `<meta charset>` sniffing, then UTF-8.

dsh-webfetch README · 中文简介：dsh-webfetch 是 DeepSeek Harness 的网页阅读插件：智能体拿到 URL 后可以直接抓取页面并提取干净的 Markdown 或纯文本（保留标题、链接、列表与代码块，剥离脚本/样式），`web_links` 可列出页面全部链接（解析为绝对地址、去重、限量），`web_feed` 可解析 RSS 2.0 / Atom 订阅源为条目清单（标题/链接/发布时间/作者/摘要/正文，处理 CDATA、HTML 实体与相对链接），`web_headers` 可用 HEAD 请求探测任意 URL 的 HTTP 状态码、响应头与重定向链而不下载正文（服务器不支持 HEAD 时自动回退 GET，非 2xx 状态照常报告），`web_table` 可把页面上的 HTML 表格提取为结构化行（表头识别、colspan/rowspan 网格展开、行列上限，定价页/参数表/对比表直接可用），`web_meta` 可读取页面自身的元数据（标题、描述、canonical、语言与字符集、robots、作者、Open Graph/article/Twitter 属性、hreflang 多语言版本、订阅源自动发现、图标与 JSON-LD 的 @type 摘要；解析失败的 JSON-LD 如实报错而不丢弃），`web_sitemap` 可从 robots.txt 的 `Sitemap:` 指令枚举整站 URL（跟随 sitemap 索引、带 lastmod/changefreq/priority、相对地址解析为绝对地址、重复折叠；抓取失败或 gzip 压缩的 sitemap 带原因列出而不中断整次查询）。零运行时依赖、只读、不发送凭证；http/https 协议限定、超时/重定向/体积/文本长度全部有上限，字符集自动识别（Content-Type → XML 声明/meta → UTF-8）；内置零依赖 http 代理支持（CONNECT 隧道 + NO_PROXY 白名单，自动读环境变量），在必须走代理的网络也能正常工作。与内置搜索互补：搜索给线索，webfetch 读正文，web_meta 读身份，web_headers 读前诊断，web_table 提数据，web_sitemap 列全站。
